name: The Report Builder
oneLiner: Turns any agent's `AgentResult[]` into a single self-contained HTML report — inlined CSS, light/dark, no external assets.
lead: One shared renderer that takes the `AgentResult[]` from any agent — tracker, API, DB — and emits a self-contained HTML report: stat tiles, a results table, colour-coded pass/fail badges, an evidence panel per agent, and an optional run matrix. It replaces ~90 report scripts that each hand-rolled their own layout, colours, and markup. Every page now draws from one CSS token set, so a single edit re-skins them all.
chore: The prior setup had ~90 report scripts, each hand-writing its own page layout, colour hexes, tables, and status labels. They drifted, so reports looked inconsistent, and changing the look meant editing every script.
instead: One kit of typed helpers — `statCards`, `table`, `badge`, `evidenceSteps`, `runMatrix` — all reading from a single `THEME_CSS` token set. Every report is byte-for-byte consistent, re-skinnable from one place, and emitted as a single standalone HTML file: CSS inlined, no external stylesheet, no network — trivial to email, archive, or screen-record.
whyItMatters: One renderer, one token set: consistent reports produced in milliseconds instead of hand-built per project. Feed it any agent's `AgentResult[]` and it composes into the same dashboard — self-contained HTML that opens anywhere, offline, unchanged years later.

howItWorks.step: `buildReportPage` takes one `ReportInput`, rolls the `AgentResult[]` into headline counts, then lays out a summary, a results table, and one evidence section per agent that carries steps.
howItWorks.explain: The report composer: `summarize()` rolls the `AgentResult[]` into `{ total, passed, failed }`, which become three `StatCard`s — the **Failed** tile only turns red (`tone: 'fail'`) when `s.failed` is non-zero, otherwise it stays `neutral` so a clean run shows no alarm colour. The Results table maps each result to a row, deriving its badge from `r.ok` and printing `r.steps?.length || 0` (the `?.` and `|| 0` guard results carrying no steps array). It then appends one **`Evidence — {agent}`** section per result that actually has steps, so passing checks with nothing to show don't clutter the page. Every piece is assembled from the shared `statCards`/`table`/`badge`/`evidenceSteps` helpers — no bespoke markup lives here.

howItWorks.step: Every page element — stat tiles, tables, status pills, run matrix, request/response evidence panels — comes from the same small set of pure string-returning helpers.
howItWorks.explain: A pure string-returning helper — no DOM, no framework — like every piece of this renderer. The column count is **clamped to 1–4** (`Math.min(Math.max(len, 1), 4)`) so one card doesn't stretch full-width and five don't crush into an unreadable row; it feeds a `grid cols-N` class the CSS knows how to lay out. A card's number is tinted only when its `tone` is set and not `'neutral'`, and it pulls the colour from the `--${tone}` CSS token rather than a hardcoded hex. Crucially **both** `it.value` and `it.label` pass through `escapeHtml`, so a value like `<3` can't inject markup into the report.

howItWorks.step: Every colour is a CSS custom property from `THEME_CSS` — `--pass`, `--fail`, `--accent` — not a hex literal per report, with a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` variant baked in.
howItWorks.explain: Every colour in the toolkit is a **CSS custom property** declared once on `:root` (`--accent`, `--pass`, `--fail`, `--warn`, `--info`), never a per-report hex — so changing `--pass` in this one block re-skins every report the kit emits. Helpers like `statCards` reference them as `var(--pass)`, so they never need to know light from dark. The `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block re-points the **same token names** to brighter values, meaning a single generated file adapts to the viewer's OS theme with no JS and no second stylesheet — which is exactly what lets each report stay self-contained.

howItWorks.step: `htmlDocument` inlines `THEME_CSS` into `<head>`, producing one standalone document — no linked stylesheet to lose, viewport meta for mobile.
howItWorks.explain: Wraps the assembled `bodyHtml` in a complete `<!doctype html>` document with `THEME_CSS` (plus any caller `extraCss`) **inlined** in a single `<style>` — there's no `<link>` to an external sheet that could 404 later, so the file renders identically offline, emailed, or opened years from now. The `<meta viewport>` lets the same document reflow on a phone. Only `title` is `escapeHtml`d, because it lands in `<title>`; the CSS and body are trusted, already-built strings. Everything a browser needs is in one file — that self-containment is the whole point of the report builder.

howItWorks.step: `runReportAgent` builds the page, writes it to disk, and returns a normal `AgentResult` pointing at the file — so a report step composes with every other agent.
howItWorks.explain: Renders and persists in one call, then returns a **normal `AgentResult`** so a report step composes with every other agent — even feeding into a larger report. `ok` is `s.failed === 0`: the report is considered passing only when none of its input results failed, so its own success mirrors what it summarizes. The absolute path from `saveReport` is carried in both `data.outPath` and an `artifacts` entry tagged `kind: 'html'`, which is how the shared evidence machinery knows to surface the rendered file as a downloadable artifact.

examples.caption: Nightly test dashboard
examples.input: The combined `AgentResult[]` of several checks — some pass, some fail — plus a pass/fail matrix across three environments.
examples.output: One HTML page titled 'QA Results Dashboard': tiles reading '12 checks · 10 passed · 2 failed', a colour-coded results table, and the matrix — all inlined in a single emailable file.

examples.caption: Re-skin every report from one token
examples.output: Every report the toolkit emits uses the new colour — no report script touched, because they all resolve the same CSS token.

examples.caption: Evidence behind a failure
examples.input: A failed check whose `steps` captured its request and response.
examples.output: An evidence panel with a red `FAIL` badge showing the exact request, status code, and trimmed response body.

underHood.heading: Summarizes the results
underHood.whenRuns: First, once every agent in the run has returned.
underHood.input: A normalized `AgentResult[]` from any domain — tracker, API, database.
underHood.output: Headline counts: agents run, passed, and failing evidence steps.

underHood.heading: Assembles sections from shared helpers
underHood.whenRuns: Right after the counts are rolled up.
underHood.input: The results plus an optional pass/fail matrix.
underHood.output: A summary, a results table, an optional run matrix, and one evidence section per agent — all from the same helper kit.

underHood.heading: Resolves every colour from one palette
underHood.whenRuns: As each helper renders its HTML.
underHood.input: Each result's tone — pass, fail, warn, info.
underHood.output: Consistent colour-coded badges and cells across the whole report, driven entirely by `THEME_CSS` tokens.

underHood.heading: Inlines into one file
underHood.output: A single self-contained document — CSS inlined, no external stylesheet — that adapts to light/dark and phone-width via media queries.

underHood.heading: Writes and reports back
underHood.whenRuns: Last, when the caller passed an output path.
underHood.output: The file is written and `runReportAgent` returns its own `AgentResult` pointing at it — ready to feed a larger report.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
Node.js (installed in step 1 below) — nothing else.
No credentials, board, database, or API key are needed for the demo below — that is the point of this module. A `.env` only matters later, if you point it at something real.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The toolkit is TypeScript on Node. One install per machine; no other runtime required.
steps.firstRun: First time on a new machine only.

steps.label: Clone and install dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the toolkit's only dependency (`dotenv`) into `node_modules`. No DB driver, no cloud SDK, no auth library — which is why the demos run credential-free.
steps.firstRun: Downloads everything (seconds — the dependency list is tiny).
steps.rerun: No-op unless the dependency list changed.

steps.label: (Optional) copy the env template — only to go live later.
steps.cmd:
cp .env.example .env
# then open .env and fill in ONLY the section you need
steps.why: Skippable for the demo — every capability is off by default and the demo runs on inline sample data regardless. `.env` matters only once you point the toolkit at a real board, service, or database.

steps.label: Run the capability check.
steps.why: Prints a one-line scorecard per capability (tracker, API, database, AI) — on/off with a reason. With an empty `.env` everything reads `(off)`, which is expected: the demo needs none of them on.

steps.label: Run the report demo — build a self-contained HTML dashboard.
steps.why: Feeds three synthetic `AgentResult`s (an API probe, a DB reconciliation, an ADO sync) plus a small pass/fail matrix into `runReportAgent()`, writing the page to `out/report/demo-dashboard.html`.
steps.rerun: Overwrites the same file with byte-identical content — the demo pins `generatedAt` to a fixed string, so reruns are deterministic and diff-clean.

steps.label: Open the dashboard.
steps.why: One self-contained HTML file — no server, no network, no external stylesheet — opens in any browser and renders correctly indefinitely. You'll see the stat tiles, colour-coded results table, evidence panels, and pass/fail matrix.

inputs.name: nothing
inputs.desc: The demo builds its `ReportInput` entirely inline (`examples/report/demo.ts`) — three synthetic `AgentResult`s and a 4-row pass/fail matrix. No credentials or files.

inputs.name: a real ReportInput (for your own use)
inputs.desc: In a real project you pass the `AgentResult[]` your own tracker/API/DB agents already returned — same shape, same builder.

outputs.name: out/report/demo-dashboard.html
outputs.desc: One self-contained HTML page: stat tiles ('3 Agents · 2 Passed · 1 Failed'), a colour-coded results table, an evidence panel per agent, and the 4×3 pass/fail matrix — all inlined, nothing external to load.

runbook.rerun: Deterministic and safe to rerun: the file is fully overwritten each run, and because the demo pins `generatedAt`, the output bytes are identical run to run. Point `runReportAgent()` at real `AgentResult`s and every rerun simply reflects your latest test results.
runbook.integrate: Import directly: `import { runReportAgent } from './agents/report'`, hand it a `ReportInput` (`{ title, subtitle, results, matrix, generatedAt }`) built from your agents' `AgentResult`s plus an output path — it returns its own `AgentResult` pointing at the file, so a report step composes with every other agent. For custom pieces, import the lower-level helpers (`statCards`, `table`, `badge`, `evidenceSteps`, `THEME_CSS`) straight from `./src/core/html`.

video.caption: A 3-4 minute screen recording: run the report demo and watch a self-contained HTML dashboard render from nothing but inline sample data.
script: Open a terminal in the qa-agent-toolkit folder, with a browser window ready alongside it.
Say: 'This is the toolkit's shared report builder. One command, one self-contained HTML file.'
Run `node -v` and `npm install` briefly; note the dependency list is just `dotenv`.
Run `npm run demo:report`; read the printed summary line: 'Rendered 3 agent result(s) — 2 passed, 1 failed'.
Run `open out/report/demo-dashboard.html`; let the browser tab load.
Point at the stat tiles at the top — Agents / Passed / Failed — and the colour coding (green/red).
Scroll to the results table; show the PASS/FAIL badges for api-probe, db-recon, ado-sync.
Scroll to an evidence panel; show the exact request/response captured for the failing db-recon check (reporting_period mismatch).
Scroll to the pass/fail matrix at the bottom; point out a 'blocked' and a 'no-run' cell.
Resize the browser narrower to show the page reflow on a phone-sized window.
Close: 'Same builder, any agent's results — swap the inline data for your own AgentResult[] and this is your dashboard.'
